title: Spectral headroom decomposition for weights/KV/activations (Memory Harmonics)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Current static headroom allocations (separate heuristics for weights, KV, and activations) are conservative and reactive, leading to wasted GPU capacity during steady-state workloads and opaque spike behavior for mixed-priority inference. We need a runtime-friendly budgeting strategy that (1) reduces average headroom allocations, (2) keeps tail OOM/latency risk bounded, and (3) is safe to roll out across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Proposal summary: Introduce a "Memory Harmonics" approach — a spectral decomposition of per-queue memory demand into persistent (weights), low-frequency KV baseline, and high-frequency activation spikes. We will compute an online multi-band budget: a persistent weight ledger + a KV baseline bank + an annealed activation spike envelope. The controller uses telemetry-derived per-tenant spectral footprints and a small stochastic margin computed from recent tail fractiles (99th/99.9th) to assign headroom bands. This enables reclaiming steady-state slack while preserving a predictable spike cushion.

Key concepts: spectral decomposition (short DFT window over memory time-series), per-tenant bank allocation, annealed safety envelope (alpha that decays with confidence), and a fast failover policy that temporarily widens the activation envelope and optionally falls back to a lighter model variant under severe pressure.

Why different: Existing tickets are heavy on reserve-ledgers and predictive headroom; Memory Harmonics emphasizes frequency-aware budgeting and an online annealing policy that automatically increases/decreases margin as traffic steadies or becomes bursty. This should be complementary to reserve-ledger work but provides a low-cost runtime knob that adapts on-minute timescales.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Window size tradeoff: 30s window gives responsiveness to microbursts but noisy spectral estimates; 5m window smooths noise but lags change. Plan: default 60s with exponential smoothing and a tunable beta in config.
- Margin rule: two parameters (alpha for stochastic margin scale, min_headroom floor) to avoid negative budgets for tiny tenants.
- Cost vs latency: reclaiming KV headroom aggressively reduces cost but increases p99 latency risk for cold-KV misses; will expose a KV-cache miss budget and require KV prefetch policy integration.
- Complexity: spectral transform adds CPU on agent; offload to dedicated telemetry aggregator in Dedicated/Private to keep the runtime lightweight.

Simulation plan: use trace-replay tool "wavefront" to run 30-day replay across 200 tenant traces (mix of interactive and batch). Metrics to collect: mean headroom by component, p50/p95/p99 token latency delta, OOM count, GPU utilization, effective cost-per-token. Goal: >=12% headroom reduction (aggregate) with p99 latency increase <5% and zero increase in OOM incidents in Canary conditions.

Rollout plan: local simulation -> integration tests -> canary on runtime-1.20 with low-risk tenants -> widen traffic and enable for Dedicated regions on a per-cluster opt-in basis -> Private deploy bundle as an optional controller. Canary includes auto-fallback to legacy budgeting if observed p99 or OOM exceeds thresholds.

Observability & controls: new dashboard panels for per-tenant harmonic bands, spectral power distribution, and active margin alpha. Add alerting on: sudden spectral power shift >x, p99 latency drift >5%, OOM burst. Provide an API toggle to adjust alpha/min_headroom per-tenant.

Acceptance criteria: Spectral headroom controller merged + simulation results meeting success thresholds + canary rollout config that includes automatic fallback and telemetry hooks.

Implementation notes: implement spectral estimator as a lightweight ring-buffer DFT (fixed 8 bins) and compute power bands (low/med/high). Controller returns three budgets and a combined guardrail to the memory allocator. Integrate with KV prefetch signals so aggressive KV reclamation can be compensated by prefetch Hints.

Links: design doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/memory-harmonics, sim dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/wavefront/harmonics-sim, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2476
acceptance_criteria: Simulated aggregate headroom reduction >= 12% across the 200-tenant trace set
No increase in OOM incidents in canary traffic; p99 token latency delta < 5% versus baseline
Controller exposes tunable alpha and min_headroom and corresponding dashboard panels
Automated fallback to legacy budgeting on breach (OOM or p99 thresholds) implemented and tested

2026-01-27 — Lina Gomez (SRE): Requested explicit rollback thresholds for p99 and OOM rate; added to acceptance criteria and alerts.
2026-01-30 — Review (Research): Suggested adding per-model spectral fingerprints to help differentiate large KV-footprint models; tracking as follow-up task.
